name: Memorizing Transformers
oneLiner: kNN lookup into a stored (k, v) memory of past tokens — an external-memory ancestor of Infini-attention and Titans.
whyFootnote: Memory-augmented lineage; not adopted as an attention layer.

name: No positional encoding at all — Haviv et al. (NoPE precursor)

source.title: Transformer Language Models without Positional Encodings Still Learn Positional Information
source.authors: Haviv, Ram, Press, Izsak, Levy (Tel Aviv / AI2)

problem: If every explicit positional encoding is the thing that breaks at unseen lengths, is it needed at all?
idea: Train causal LMs up to 1.3B on the Pile with no positional encoding. Perplexity is competitive; probes recover absolute position from the hidden states. The causal mask itself leaks position (each token can count what it sees) — bidirectional models cannot do this.
buys: Empirical licence for NoPE and for the 2025 NoPE-global / RoPE-local hybrids
Removes the component that breaks past training length
costs: Slightly worse than the best PE at every scale in the paper
Implicit position is fragile at scale; length generalisation is not automatic
Decoder-only; no locality prior to exploit

rag32k.why: trained-length QA gains nothing from dropping RoPE; slightly worse at every scale

coding128k.why: as global layers in a hybrid

agent1m.why: as the global layers (Command R7B, Llama 4 iRoPE), never alone

pickWhen.verdict: The hint that matured into NoPE (2023), Command R7B / iRoPE (2024–25) and DroPE (Dec 2025). Note the co-author: Ofir Press, from ALiBi.

name: KERPLE (and Sandwich) — kernelised relative bias for extrapolation

source.title: KERPLE: Kernelized Relative Positional Embedding for Length Extrapolation

problem: ALiBi's fixed linear slope decays too aggressively; T5's log-bucketed bias extrapolates but degrades past ~4× the training length and is ~10% slower — KERPLE keeps the log shape with 2 parameters per head instead of 32.
idea: Replace the linear penalty with conditionally-positive-definite kernels of |m−n| (log / power variants, two learned parameters per head); Sandwich later gives a parameter-free sinusoid-derived bias.
buys: Better extrapolation perplexity than ALiBi/T5 with negligible parameters
costs: Additive bias → no fast-attention path until FlexAttention-style kernels
Locality prior limits retrieval; never adopted by frontier models

chatbot2k.why: a softer learned ALiBi; fine at 2K but the additive bias needs FlexAttention-style kernels

rag32k.why: the locality prior discounts far chunks; retrieval over 32K suffers like ALiBi

coding128k.why: cross-file recall needs far tokens; the kernel-shaped bias still decays them

agent1m.why: a distance-decayed bias makes 1M effectively local; never adopted by frontier models

pickWhen.verdict: The ALiBi → KERPLE → FIRE lineage: the learned-bias branch that lost to RoPE + scaling.

name: FlashAttention — exact attention, IO-aware
aka: FA1 / FA2 / FA3; fused tiled attention with online softmax

source.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
source.authors: Dao, Fu, Ermon, Rudra, Ré (Stanford / Buffalo)

secondary.label: FlashAttention-3 (Shah, Bikshandi, Zhang, Thakkar, Ramani, Dao) — Hopper, FP8
PyTorch 2.0 makes it a default SDPA backend

firstShipped.model: LLaMA-1 — first named open model using it (xformers attention 'uses the backward from Dao et al. (2022)'); PyTorch 2.0 made it a default SDPA backend three weeks later; MPT-7B first to advertise it

problem: Exact attention was slow not because of FLOPs but because the n×n score matrix is written to and read from HBM — memory-bandwidth-bound and O(n²) memory. Long sequences were impractical even where compute was affordable.
idea: Change nothing about the maths. Tile Q, K, V into SRAM-sized blocks, compute softmax online (running max and sum), never materialise the n×n matrix, and recompute scores in the backward pass instead of storing them. FA2 fixed work partitioning (25–40% → 50–73% of A100 peak); FA3 added Hopper asynchrony and FP8.
buys: Same outputs, O(n) memory, a 2–4× faster attention kernel — end-to-end up to 3× on GPT-2 vs the HuggingFace baseline (1.7× vs Megatron), 15% on BERT-large; first Transformer to beat chance on Path-X 16K
Made 32K–128K dense-attention training and serving economical — the reason the 2020 approximations stopped mattering at ordinary lengths
Ecosystem-level: a default backend in PyTorch 2.0, in every serving stack
costs: A systems change, not a math change: compute is still O(n²) and the KV cache is untouched — at 1M tokens you still need GQA/MLA, windows or linear layers
Hand-written hardware-specific kernels (Ampere → Hopper), slow to port to new accelerators and to new attention variants — biases (ALiBi) and sparse patterns lagged for a year
Backward pass trades extra FLOPs for bandwidth; numerics differ slightly (accumulation order, FP8 in FA3)

chatbot2k.why: always, when a kernel exists — free quality-wise

rag32k.why: the kernel that made dense 32K economical; the 2020 approximations stopped mattering here

agent1m.why: necessary but not sufficient — the KV bill needs a math change on top

pickWhen.verdict: The timeline's hinge: a kernel made exact cheap, the field un-learned approximation for a while, and every later sparse design (NSA, DSA) is written to be 'hardware-aligned' because of the lesson.

name: xPos — RoPE with exponential decay (LEX Transformer)

source.title: A Length-Extrapolatable Transformer
source.authors: Sun, Dong, Patra, Ma, Huang, Benhaim, Chaudhary, Song, Wei (Microsoft)
source.evidence: [v1] Tue, 20 Dec 2022 18:56:20 UTC (same day as Sandwich, 2212.10356)

problem: RoPE's attention resolution becomes noisy at long relative distances; wanted RoPE-quality interpolation with ALiBi-like extrapolation.
idea: Multiply RoPE by a per-dimension decay ξ^{m−n} so scores decay smoothly with distance; add blockwise causal attention at inference.
buys: Better long-length perplexity than RoPE/ALiBi in the paper
The decay idea reappears as RetNet's γ (same group)
costs: Hard locality prior hurts long-range retrieval; ξ^n needs numerical offset tricks
No frontier adoption — RoPE + θ-scaling won

chatbot2k.why: the decay barely bites at 2K, so it is RoPE with offset tricks; pick RoPE

rag32k.why: the exponential decay discounts far chunks; retrieval over the 32K suffers

coding128k.why: the hard locality prior fades far files; use RoPE + θ-scaling

agent1m.why: ξ^{m−n} decay makes 1M effectively local; whole-context recall is lost

pickWhen.verdict: The bridge from RoPE to RetNet's decay; not a production pick.

name: H3 → Hyena — attention-free long convolutions (SSM lineage)

source.title: Hungry Hungry Hippos: Towards Language Modeling with State Space Models (H3); Hyena Hierarchy (2302.10866, 21 Feb 2023)
source.authors: Fu, Dao, Saab, Thomas, Rudra, Ré (Stanford); Poli et al.
source.evidence: H3 [v1] Wed, 28 Dec 2022 17:56:03 UTC; Hyena [v1] Tue, 21 Feb 2023 18:29:25 UTC

problem: Can O(n²) attention be replaced outright? SSMs were fast but bad at recall/comparison.
idea: H3: a shift SSM plus a diagonal SSM with multiplicative gating gives SSMs recall; Hyena: long implicit convolutions via FFT (O(n log n)) with data-controlled gating; FlashConv is the FlashAttention move applied to convolutions.
buys: Sub-quadratic; ~1B-scale parity claims; 100× faster than FlashAttention at 64K
costs: FFT convolutions use tensor cores poorly
Weak in-context recall/copying vs attention; needs hybrids
No frontier text LLM adopted it — the text instance stopped at StripedHyena-7B (Dec 2023); the durable uses are long low-density signals (Evo for DNA)

chatbot2k.why: exact attention is cheap at 2K; FFT convolutions waste tensor cores for nothing

rag32k.why: weak in-context recall/copying — retrieval QA is exactly what long convolutions cannot do

coding128k.why: cross-file recall needs attention-grade copying, which long convolutions lack

pickWhen.verdict: The attention-free branch before Mamba; it lost on recall and on tensor-core utilisation.

name: RWKV — Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV-4 checkpoints, a year before the paper)

source.title: RWKV-4-Pile checkpoints on Hugging Face (BlinkDL); paper 'RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era'
source.evidence: HF uploads 'RWKV-4-Pile-169M-20220807-8023.pth' / '430M-20220808-8066.pth' committed 2022-08-17 (repo README later lists 'RWKV-4-Pile-1B5-20220903'); the paper's arXiv v1 is [v1] Mon, 22 May 2023 13:57:41 UTC — dated here by first public appearance, per the timeline's rule

firstShipped.model: RWKV-4-Pile 169M/430M (its own open model line; HF transformers 4.29 added it 10 May 2023)

problem: Quadratic attention and a growing KV cache; wanted RNN-style O(1) per-token inference with transformer-style parallel training.
idea: Replace attention with a linear time-mix (WKV) plus channel-mix; trainable in parallel, run as an RNN at inference.
buys: Linear time, constant memory, no KV cache; competitive with same-size transformers up to 14B in the paper
Fully open weights and code; the community proof that the RNN was not dead
costs: Fixed state → weak exact recall / needle retrieval; prompt-order sensitivity
Kernel and serving ecosystem less mature; the paper is a post-hoc description of RWKV-4

coding128k.why: a fixed state cannot hold 128K of code for exact cross-file recall

pickWhen.verdict: The RNN revival shipped quietly in Aug 2022, nine months before its paper and the same spring GQA squeezed the cache — the two answers to the KV bill: shrink it, or abolish it.
